title: a-question-and-its-ticket-name-each-other-and-an-answer-names-what-it-spawned
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; codemother owns the care of the code; the question store and the ticket files are records of truth in the commons gated by the artifact door; cairn/tools/question has users, not owners (Law 6).
ruling: none — a decision is a question bound to its ticket (ticket 9adc6fddf185). Akien's words of 2026-09-14 are the spec and ride from_idea verbatim; the cast opened no question because none of its choices is a spec choice.
decision_verbatim: yes ticket. as to the loop residue point, if a question is about a ticket, it should have a bidirectional link. and we should explicitly say "and the answer spawned x, y and z new questions" in some jasonic way that's not prose
pre_approval: none claimed — stands at his review queue; 'yes ticket' orders the cast, not the build.
intention: A question about a ticket and the ticket point at each other by construction, and an answer states in JSON — never in prose — which new questions it spawned, including the explicit statement that it spawned none.
why: Law 5 (the ticket's address carries what a mind needs now — its questions and their answers — without correlating a second store by hand); Law 4 (the loop's round-trip — 'if the answer does, we keep going around' — is a field the door refuses to leave unsaid and a sieve that reds a broken link, not CC's discipline to open a follow-up); Law 7 (a link with one end is a record that can silently disagree with itself; the reverse traversal is what makes the disagreement loud); Law 1 (the spawned list is the compiled answer to 'did that settle it?', asked once).
how: In cairn/tools/question (the door): (1) open_question(ticket=<id>) appends the new id to the ticket record's `questions` list through the artifact door in the same act, so ticket.questions and question.ticket are the two ends of one link tuple (I-universal-addressing-and-bidirectional-links: 'the tuple is always bidirectional by construction'); a follow-up born of an answer lands on the ticket the same way. (2) A question raised at /intent, before a ticket id exists, binds to the intent berth path; when /sorted files the ticket carrying that intent_berth, the filing rebinds every such question to the ticket id and lists it — charter edge (a) closes. (3) The answer verb takes `spawned` as a REQUIRED field — a list of the follow-up questions (each opened born_of the answered one, on the same ticket) or the literal empty list, and the door refuses an answer that does not say; the answered record carries `spawned: [ids]` (the field `follow_ups` becomes this — the name says what he said: 'the answer spawned x, y and z'), and `spawned: []` is a recorded claim that the answer settled the question, not a default — charter edge (c) becomes a statement instead of a judgement nobody made. (4) A sieve in build_inspector, `question_links_agree`, reds a ticket that lists a question naming another ticket, a question naming a ticket that does not list it, or an answered question whose spawned ids are not open records born_of it — the reverse traversal the link tuple exists for. (5) `cairn question list <ticket>` and the inbox render the tree (question → spawned → spawned) from the records, and `cairn operator show artifact <ticket>` shows the ticket's questions beside it.
falsifier: DONE when: (1) `cairn question open --ticket <id>` leaves the id in the ticket file's `questions` list, written through the artifact door (journal shows the ticket path in the same act), and a follow-up born of an answer appears there too; (2) `cairn question answer <qid> "<words>"` without `--spawned` is REFUSED; `--spawned none` records `spawned: []`; `--spawned "<q>" ...` records the born ids in `spawned` and on the ticket, each born_of the answered one; (3) a question opened against an intent berth path is rebound to the ticket id when /sorted files a ticket carrying that intent_berth, and the BUILDME gate then holds the crossing on it; (4) `question_links_agree` reds a hand-broken link in either direction and an answered question whose spawned id is absent, reads clean over the live corpus after the build, and a revert of the sieve lets the broken link through (hollow-proof); (5) the hollow reading finds every written file load-bearing. Horizon: one build. WRONG INTENT if the ticket file's journal becomes mostly link maintenance — then the ticket side is derived at read time and only the question side stored.
traces_to: Law 5 (the ticket's address carries what a mind needs now — its questions and their answers — without correlating a second store by hand); Law 4 (the loop's round-trip — 'if the answer does, we keep going around' — is a field the door refuses to leave unsaid and a sieve that reds a broken link, not CC's discipline to open a follow-up); Law 7 (a link with one end is a record that can silently disagree with itself; the reverse traversal is what makes the disagreement loud); Law 1 (the spawned list is the compiled answer to 'did that settle it?', asked once).

watchme.enough: 50 question events (opens + answers) after the build with ZERO question_links_agree lacks over the live corpus, AND at least 5 answers carrying a non-empty `spawned` (the loop went around, recorded as JSON) — or ONE lack over a record the door itself wrote, which is the finding: the door maintained one end and not the other, the WRONG-INTENT clause.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: the event count, the lack count by predicate, the histogram of `spawned` lengths, and every /intent-born question rebound (or still bound to a berth path).
watchme.nexus: the what-Akien-decides tree — the same lane the throughput probe (no_crossing_with_an_open_question) reads; this probe measures the lane's INTEGRITY (do both ends agree) beside its throughput.
watchme.consumer: Akien, and the universal-addressing intention's builder when the link-tuple discipline is widened to follow_ons/depends_on.

gates_bound: code-seam gate-set: BUILDME rides the intent berth and the sorted berth (buildme_rides_the_intent, buildme_rides_the_sorted) and the_ticket_has_every_answer_it_needs (no question stands open on this ticket — none is opened). PROVEME: proofs sealed green with current fingerprint; hollow reading over every writes_to file; proof_coverage naming a tooth per falsifier clause; the sieve's self-reference tooth (revert question_links_agree, a broken link passes, the tooth reds). PROVED: verdict artifact against the falsifier. Feeds back to origin on failure — a red at PROVEME kicks the ticket to BUILDME through the emit chokepoint; a link the sieve cannot classify kicks to Akien as a question on this ticket.

owed_physics: nothing today keeps ticket.questions and question.ticket in agreement, and nothing makes 'this answer spawned nothing' a statement rather than an absence; both are this ticket's build (the door writes both ends, the answer verb requires `spawned`, question_links_agree reds a disagreement).

cast_checks.assumption_check: Load-bearing and settled by measurement or by his words, not left standing: (1) the ticket file may be rewritten by the question door — measured: the artifact door journals ticket writes with verb cast today (clearance.clear writes cursors back the same way), so appending to `questions` is one more journaled cast; (2) `spawned` required-explicit is my read of 'explicitly say the answer spawned x, y and z in some jsonic way' — the field already exists as `follow_ups` (populated only when CC passes --follow-up); the delta is that the door refuses an answer that does not state its spawn, so `[]` is a claim CC made and the journal shows who made it — a design detail under his words, not a spec choice (memory blocker-is-foundation-not-authority), recorded here rather than asked; (3) the /intent-born question binds to the intent berth path until /sorted's filing rebinds it — the rebind lives in the filing step because that is the one act that knows both the berth and the new id; (4) the sieve is a build_inspector sieve because that is where every other 'two records must agree' check lives (history_integrity, constraint_enforcement_holds).
cast_checks.missing_check: Wrapped: the door's two writes (question side, ticket side), the rebind at /sorted filing, the required `spawned` field and its CLI spelling (`--spawned none` | `--spawned "<q>" ...`), the sieve's three predicates (ticket lists a question naming another ticket; question names a ticket that does not list it; answered question whose spawned ids are not open records born_of it), the renderers (list, inbox, operator show). Not wrapped and said so: (a) whether an /intent-born question that never reaches /sorted (the intent was killed) stays open forever — my read: it stays, bound to the berth path, and the inbox shows it under the berth; a killed intent with an open question is a signal, not litter. (b) tickets' `follow_ons`/`depends_on` are the same one-way shape and are NOT touched — a follow-on for the universal-addressing intention, named in the bullets.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: DONE when: (1) `cairn question open --ticket <id>` leaves the id in the ticket file's `questions` list, written through the artifact door (journal shows the ticket path in the same act), and a follow-up born of an answer appears there too; (2) `cairn question answer <qid> "<words>"` without `--spawned` is REFUSED; `--spawned none` records `spawned: []`; `--spawned "<q>" ...` records the born ids in `spawned` and on the ticket, each born_of the answered one; (3) a question opened against an intent berth path is rebound to the ticket id when /sorted files a ticket carrying that intent_berth, and the BUILDME gate then holds the crossing on it; (4) `question_links_agree` reds a hand-broken link in either direction and an answered question whose spawned id is absent, reads clean over the live corpus after the build, and a revert of the sieve lets the broken link through (hollow-proof); (5) the hollow reading finds every written file load-bearing. Horizon: one build. WRONG INTENT if the ticket file's journal becomes mostly link maintenance — then the ticket side is derived at read time and only the question side stored.
cast_checks.collision_check: Whys compared, none exclusive-and-terminal. (1) I-universal-addressing-and-bidirectional-links (Akien 2026-08-23): its why is that a link with one end cannot be traversed back when the far end moves or voids; this ticket is that design applied to one file-side link (ticket↔question) — not a rival, an instance. (2) The artifact door (30531f6e1c5d): its why is that a record changes only through a journaled door; the question door already rides it, and the ticket-side write rides it too — no second writer. (3) The question tool's charter edges (a) and (c): this ticket closes them; the charter's filed_edges are amended in the build to say so, through the charter verb. (4) Law 1 vs. storing both ends: storing a derivable value looks like re-deriving the settled, but the why of Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs NOW, readable cold) wins for a record a human cats — the sieve is what keeps two copies from becoming two truths (Law 7).
cast_checks.builder_check: What a Haiku-level builder needs, carried here: the door is cairn/tools/question/question.py (open_question, answer, _write riding cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write); the ticket lives at CairnCommons/tickets/<id>-<slug>.json and its `questions` field is a list of open-<12hex> ids; the ticket write goes through door.write(path, content, verb="cast", why=...) exactly as clearance.clear does for cursors; `follow_ups` is renamed `spawned` on NEW records and the reader accepts both names on old ones (the four live records under 9adc6fddf185 carry follow_ups: [] and are not rewritten — Law 7); the CLI spelling is `--spawned none` or `--spawned "<q>"` (repeatable), and `answer()` takes `spawned: list[str] | None` where None is refused; the /intent side: open_question(ticket=<intent berth path>) is legal when the path exists under ~/.cairn/devices/skill_block/0/berths/intent/, and skills/sorted's filing step (the ticket write at SKILL.md §5) calls question.rebind(berth_path, ticket_id) which rewrites each such question's `ticket` and appends its id to the ticket; the sieve registers in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py beside history_integrity and reads both directories; the BUILDME gate (open_for) is unchanged — it reads question.ticket, and the sieve is what guarantees the ticket side agrees. Left to the builder: the sieve's exact lack wording, whether `cairn question list` renders the tree with indentation or with born_of lines (both are fine).

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Looked. Smaller: derive ticket.questions at read time from question.ticket and never store it — one end, no drift possible. Rejected because he asked for the link to be bidirectional and Law 5 wants the ticket file to carry its questions where a cold reader (cat, grep, the inbox) sees them without running a query; the sieve is what keeps two stored ends honest, which is the universal-addressing design already in force. Smaller for the spawn: keep `follow_ups` as is and merely document it — but a list that is empty by default cannot say 'settled', which is the residue he pointed at.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: In-house: I-universal-addressing-and-bidirectional-links (Akien 2026-08-23) — the link tuple, reverse traversal on change; the question tool's own charter edges (a) and (c), filed 2026-09-14, are exactly this ticket's scope; the artifact door (30531f6e1c5d) already journals the ticket write; tickets carry `follow_ons` and `depends_on` as one-way lists today (the same drift, not fixed here). Field: bidirectional links in Roam/Obsidian backlinks — derived, not stored; ADR 'supersedes/superseded-by' pairs — stored both ends, checked by lint.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: (a) That the ticket file may be rewritten by the question door — it is a record of truth and the door journals it with verb cast, so yes, but the ticket_inspector's field checks must accept a `questions` list that grows. (b) That 'spawned' as a required field will be filled honestly — `[]` is as easy to type as before; the difference is that it is now a recorded claim CC made, visible in the journal, rather than an absence. (c) That a question raised at /intent is rare enough that the rebind can live in /sorted's filing step rather than in a separate verb.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: None exclusive-and-terminal. Distinction recorded: tickets' `follow_ons`/`depends_on` are also one-way today; this ticket does not touch them — the link-tuple discipline they need is the universal-addressing intention's, and widening the sieve to them is a follow-on, not a hidden scope.
challenge_at_birth.back_up: proceed — his words of 2026-09-14 are the spec: 'if a question is about a ticket, it should have a bidirectional link. and we should explicitly say and the answer spawned x, y and z new questions in some jasonic way that's not prose'.
